answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated escrowed trades with counterparties who already have stake at risk. After each trade, both sides sign the outcome; disputes trigger slashing of the dishonest party’s bond, while reputation grows slowly across distinct partners. A sybil can wander through shale-thin identities, but each new account must lock fresh capital and build history, so splitting identities multiplies the required stake and delays access to valuable work. A delta of cheap accounts cannot cheaply manufacture trusted counterparties.
